questions.q: Which pair of reagents gives tert-butyl methyl ether in good yield by Williamson synthesis?
questions.explain: The halide carbon is where SN2 attack happens, so it must be methyl or primary; the bulky tert-butyl group belongs on the alkoxide side. Methoxide with tert-butyl bromide gives only an alkene by E2.

questions.q: Sodium methoxide is warmed with tert-butyl bromide. The main organic product is:
questions.explain: With a tertiary halide the alkoxide acts as a base and removes a β-hydrogen instead of attacking the crowded carbon, so E2 is the only reaction: CH₃ONa + (CH₃)₃CBr → CH₂=C(CH₃)₂ + CH₃OH + NaBr.

questions.q: Which combination is used to prepare anisole (methoxybenzene)?
questions.explain: The aryl carbon cannot undergo SN2, so the aryl part must come from the phenoxide and the methyl part from CH₃I. Phenol is first converted to sodium phenoxide with NaOH.

questions.q: (R)-2-Bromobutane is treated with sodium methoxide. Which description of the products is correct?
questions.explain: SN2 backside attack inverts the stereocentre, and the priority order (O > ethyl > methyl > H) is unchanged, so R becomes S. Because the halide is secondary, E2 competes and alkenes form alongside the ether.
